---
title: Breakpoints
description: Shared responsive breakpoints for JavaScript and CSS.
---

The theme package exports a single set of breakpoints so JavaScript logic and CSS media queries stay in sync.

## Import

```tsx
import { BREAKPOINTS, type Breakpoint } from "@puzzle-ui/theme";
```

## Values

| Breakpoint | Value  |
| ---------- | ------ |
| `compact`  | `480`  |
| `tablet`   | `768`  |
| `desktop`  | `1024` |
| `hd`       | `1440` |

Values are numbers in pixels. The `Breakpoint` type is the union of the keys: `"compact" | "tablet" | "desktop" | "hd"`.

## Usage in JavaScript

```tsx
import { BREAKPOINTS } from "@puzzle-ui/theme";

const isDesktop = window.matchMedia(
  `(min-width: ${BREAKPOINTS.desktop}px)`,
).matches;
```

## Usage in CSS

The `tablet`, `desktop`, and `hd` breakpoints are also available as [design tokens](/docs/theme/tokens#breakpoints), emitted as `--puzzle-breakpoint-tablet`, `--puzzle-breakpoint-desktop`, and `--puzzle-breakpoint-hd`. Note that CSS custom properties cannot be used inside media query conditions, so media queries should use the pixel values directly; the token variables are useful for layout calculations such as `max-width`.

```css
.layout {
  max-width: var(--puzzle-breakpoint-desktop);
}

@media (min-width: 768px) {
  .layout {
    padding: var(--puzzle-space-8);
  }
}
```
